Taking remove-legacy-start-menu-shortcut-in-both-instal. Starting the 2.1.2 release now. One question about the final step, asked up front so it does not block me later — everything before it I can do without an answer.

WHERE THINGS STAND. Main is 8e32a73010a16584bb352a334ec94e78bfe03c9d in all three refs, one commit past the 2.1.1 release commit, and that commit is claude-theme's landed fix. Version metadata still reads 2.1.1. No v2.1.2 tag anywhere.

I READ THE LANDED FIX AND IT DOES ADDRESS MY FINDING CORRECTLY. It factors the cleanup into an orgtreeRemoveLegacyShortcuts macro that sets SetShellVarContext explicitly: for an all-users install it cleans the all-users scope, switches to current and cleans the per-user scope, then restores all so the install section that follows is unaffected; for a per-user install it cleans only current. That is exactly the gap I measured.

THE REGRESSION IS BETTER THAN THE ONE IT REPLACES, with one honest limit. tests/installer-shortcut-scope.test.mjs parses the real macro out of installer.nsh and interprets its SetShellVarContext and Delete lines against two isolated fixture Start Menu roots, asserting both legacy entries are removed in the right scopes, that the branded Orgtree.lnk survives in both, and that the all-users branch restores the all-users context. That satisfies "resolved runtime paths rather than source-text matching" far better than the old grep did. The limit worth stating: it is still a JavaScript simulation of NSIS semantics, so it cannot catch a wrong assumption about how electron-builder sets the ambient context, nor any NSIS-specific quirk. Only a real install can. That is why the install step is load-bearing here rather than a formality.

I HAVE CAPTURED THE BEFORE-STATE, which makes this machine the actual test subject:
  EXISTS  %APPDATA%\...\Start Menu\Programs\Orgtree v2.lnk   legacy, dated 2026-09-09  <- must be GONE after 2.1.2
  EXISTS  %APPDATA%\...\Start Menu\Programs\Orgtree.lnk      branded, icon runtime-icons\orgtree-eye.ico  <- must REMAIN
  EXISTS  %PROGRAMDATA%\...\Programs\Orgtree\Orgtree.lnk     current all-users  <- must REMAIN
  absent  the three other legacy paths
  installed Orgtree.exe FileVersion 2.1.1
So the fix has something real to delete here, and a real thing it must not touch. I will re-read all six paths after the install and diff against this snapshot.

MY QUESTION. The item description says I should "install it, restart Orgtree, and verify the running packaged identity". For 2.1.1 you owned install and restart and I deliberately did not touch them. Restarting Orgtree tears down the backend that is hosting this organization, which is the process my own turn runs through, so I want your explicit word rather than an inference. Which of these do you want:
(a) I do everything including running the installer and the restart, accepting that the restart interrupts the org, and I verify the shortcut state and running identity afterwards.
(b) I do everything up to and including publishing, then hand you the installer path and hashes and my before-snapshot, you install and restart as you did for 2.1.1, and I verify the shortcut state and the running identity afterwards from the restart notice.
(c) Something else you prefer.

I would recommend (b), for the same reason it was right last time: you own the restart mechanism, and an agent restarting the host it is running inside is a worse failure mode than one extra handoff. But the verification that actually closes acceptance conditions 1 and 4 is mine either way, and I have the before-snapshot to do it against.

Proceeding meanwhile with: private worktree from 8e32a73 with a real private node_modules, version bump to 2.1.2 and release notes, commit, typecheck plus the full root, renderer and python sweeps against the recorded 2.1.1 failure baseline, package, the two generated manifests, and then independent review by runtime-verify, who is already the named reviewer and reviewed the fix itself. I will not land, tag or publish without your slot.
[END MAIL]
